title: Graph Learning at Scale: Characterizing and Optimizing Pre-Propagation GNNs
problem: Pre-propagation GNNs (PP-GNNs), which decouple feature propagation from training as a preprocessing step, suffer from data loading as their dominant bottleneck (88-91% of training time) and face severe scalability challenges from input expansion (K(R+1)x larger inputs).
motivation: PP-GNNs theoretically solve neighbor explosion in graph sampling but their practical efficiency is largely unexplored. Data loading from storage and large expanded input sizes prevent them from realizing their theoretical advantages.
method: To reduce data loading bottlenecks, the approach optimizes how data moves from storage to the GPU. It uses chunk reshuffling—organizing data in larger blocks instead of individual rows—which lets the GPU prepare its own training batches. It overlaps reading from storage with GPU computation by prefetching the next batch while the current one processes, and uses GPU Direct Storage (GDS) to connect the GPU directly to fast storage for very large graphs. Additionally, it adjusts the training process using mini-batch gradient descent and chunk-based sampling strategies to handle the expanded input sizes.
key_novelty: The key finding is that data loading, not computation, is the bottleneck in pre-propagation GNN training, and chunk reshuffling—organizing data in larger blocks instead of individual rows—lets the GPU prepare training batches without fine-grained per-row shuffling.
contributions: Comprehensive characterization comparing PP-GNNs vs graph-sampling methods in efficiency, scalability, and accuracy
Identification of data loading (88-91% of time) as the key bottleneck
Chunk reshuffling technique enabling coarser I/O with GPU-side batch assembly
Double-buffer prefetching overlapping data loading with computation
GPU Direct Storage (GDS) integration for large-graph scalability
15x average training throughput speedup over PP-GNN baselines
Up to 100x speedup versus sampling-based GNNs on large graph benchmarks
workloads: Node classification on large graphs (ogbn-papers100M, MAG240M)

metrics.vs_sampling_gnn: Up to 100x speedup on large graph benchmarks

limitations: Chunk reshuffling provides coarser shuffle quality than fully random; GPU Direct Storage requires NVMe with GDS support; benefits depend on storage bandwidth; not evaluated on dynamic graphs.
primary_theme: Graph Neural Network Training / I/O Optimization
